# Avatar

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 2 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a person or an account: a picture, initials or an icon in a circle. It is as tall as a
control of the same `size`, so an avatar and a Button in one row line up.

```tsx
import { AvatarFallback, AvatarImage, AvatarRoot, AvatarSkeleton } from 'topclassui/avatar'

<AvatarRoot size="lg">
  <AvatarImage src="/team/omar.jpg" alt="Omar Abed" />
  <AvatarFallback>OA</AvatarFallback>
</AvatarRoot>
```

Every part is a flat export: `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback` and
`AvatarSkeleton`; there is no `Avatar`. Only `AvatarRoot` takes `size`. Always render the
fallback: the image is laid over it, so it shows until the image paints, with no JavaScript.
Initials are one or two characters: a longer string is cut at the edge of the circle.

**A picture that fails.** `AvatarImage` is the one client part. Once the page hydrates, a
picture that fails, before or after the script ran, takes `data-error` and turns
transparent: the img stays, so its `alt` still names the avatar, and the fallback shows. A
new `src` or `srcSet` starts again, and so does a picture that loads. Before hydration the
browser's broken mark shows in the corner, and the alt text is never drawn. Your own
`onError`, `onLoad` and `ref` still reach the img, and `onError` runs once for a picture
that failed before the script ran too.

**What it costs.** An avatar of initials or an icon stays server HTML, with no client part.
The avatar re-exports `AvatarImage`, so a page that imports it may still load that one small
file. Every avatar with an image hydrates: a table of fifty rows with pictures is fifty
client parts.

**A picture with transparency.** The initials show through it. Leave `AvatarFallback` out, or
pass `className="bg-surface"` to `AvatarImage`, which also hides the fallback while the
picture loads.

**next/image.** Pass it as `render`. It carries its own `src` and `alt`, and takes the
classes that fill the circle:

```tsx
import Image from 'next/image'

<AvatarRoot size="lg">
  <AvatarImage render={<Image src="/team/omar.jpg" alt="Omar Abed" width={48} height={48} />} />
  <AvatarFallback>OA</AvatarFallback>
</AvatarRoot>
```

**Naming it.** The fallback is decorative: it renders `aria-hidden="true"`, so the image's
`alt` is the one name a screen reader reads. `alt` is required; pass `alt=""` when the name
is written beside the avatar. An avatar with no image and no name written beside it takes
`aria-label` on `AvatarRoot`, which then renders `role="img"` itself:

```tsx
<AvatarRoot aria-label="Lina Haddad">
  <AvatarFallback>LH</AvatarFallback>
</AvatarRoot>
```

Pass `aria-hidden={false}` to `AvatarFallback` only if the initials themselves should be read.

**Base UI.** Not used. Its `avatar` Image keeps a failed picture mounted, but it needs Base
UI's own Root, which would take the root and the fallback to the client as well.

**Not built:** `shape`, `bordered`, `status`, `clickable` and `onLoadingStatusChange`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AvatarRoot,
  AvatarImage,
  AvatarFallback,
  AvatarSkeleton,
} from 'topclassui/avatar'
```

## Props

Required: `alt` or `render` on `AvatarImage`. Every other prop below is optional.

### AvatarRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The parts: an AvatarFallback, and an AvatarImage when there is a picture. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The control scale on both axes, so an avatar lines up with a button of the same size; custom emits no size classes. |

### AvatarImage

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alt` | **yes**, or `render` | `string` | - | Who the picture shows. Pass an empty string when the name is written beside it. |
| `render` | **yes**, or `alt` | `ReactElement` | - | Render the picture as another element, such as next/image, which carries its own src and alt. |

### AvatarFallback

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Initials or an Svg icon, shown until the image paints. Decorative: aria-hidden unless you pass false. |

### AvatarSkeleton

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The control scale on both axes, so an avatar lines up with a button of the same size; custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
